docs.title: MatCore
docs.text:
Material Core (MatCore) is a metadata standard for computational materials science. MatCore represents key aspects of a material-focused computation to make it understandable to the broad materials research community. It provides pragmatic and workable guidelines for documentation of materials data.

MatCore is developed as a grassroots effort by experts in first principles calculations (DFT, GW), molecular dynamics, phase field, machine learning for materials, and related fields.

Browse the standard · Submit feedback

The MatCore effort is funded by the National Science Foundation, Division of Materials Research (DMR) through Award #2404283 and supported through the KIM Initiative.

docs.title: 0000 — Move the standard to a Git repository; YAML as source of truth
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-31. Status: accepted.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The standard was a Google Doc, manually edited, converted to HTML by a script from a .docx export. Not programmatically accessible; two sources of truth.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Public GitHub organization matcore-standard and single repository matcore (schema + docs + tools; split later if needed).
  • Standard expressed in regular MatCore YAML (one file per section) validated by a JSON-Schema meta-schema written in YAML. No LinkML dependency (may be revisited; keep YAML regular so a translation stays mechanical).
  • Baseline migration first, tagged; every subsequent change (units, typed fields, community feedback) as separate PRs referencing decision records.
  • Static site (MkDocs Material, GitHub Pages, mike for versions). Tools as one Python package, run in-browser via Pyodide.
  • Licenses CC BY 4.0 (text/schema), Apache-2.0 (code). Releases get Zenodo DOIs.
  • Google Doc frozen on tagging the baseline.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Committee reviews changes as PRs; decisions live in docs/decisions/. Generated chapters are never hand-edited.

docs.title: MatCore Metadata Schema — Change List for Units Handling
docs.text:
Status (2026-10-31, see 0004): Part A accepted. Part B: B1, B3, B4 (unit), B6, B7, B8, B10, B11 accepted; B2 (added note), B4 (Ė symbol), B5, B9 proposed, not decided; B12 no action. A6 proposed, not decided.

A3.3 removed 2026-10-31: referred to a DFT computation-parameter that does not exist; the MD entry is covered by A4.1.

A7.4 amended 2026-10-31: grid-spacing and time-step-size are typed properties (Length, Time; Annex U symbols only, recommended units m and s), not generic parameters; the field-variable value line is removed because field-variable has no value. Annex U Rule 4 amended 2026-10-31: the x-gnu: escape applies to the unit of a generic parameter or of any other subproperty whose Kind the schema declares as any. Nondimensional domain-size, grid-spacing and time-step-size are covered by 0003.

Part A implements the units design (explicit unit on every dimensioned property; schema declares Quantity kind + Recommended unit; no default unit is ever implied). Part B contains independent fixes to existing content. Apply Part B even if Part A is deferred.

Line references are to the draft MatCore_Dev.docx; "old" text is quoted so each spot can be found with Find.

Notation: Quantity kind and Recommended unit replace the current Standard units phrase everywhere. Recommended unit is informative only.

docs.title: A1. General rule (§1.3 Format)
docs.text:
A1.1 Find the bullet:

When a value has physical units, either the required unit must be specified, or a field provided to define the value units.

Replace with:

Units of physical quantities. Every property whose value is a physical quantity (i.e. whose Quantity kind is neither "dimensionless" nor "inapplicable") SHALL carry a unit subproperty in the metadata instance. The value of unit SHALL be a symbol from the MatCore Unit Table (Annex U) whose quantity kind is compatible with the property's declared Quantity kind. A property value without a unit, or with a unit incompatible with its Quantity kind, is non-conformant; no default unit is ever implied. The Recommended unit listed for each property is informative and does not affect how values are interpreted. Quantities of dimension one use the reserved symbol dimensionless; plane angles use an angle unit (rad or degree). Where the meaning of a value depends on a convention that a unit cannot express (e.g. inclusion of a factor 2π in reciprocal lengths, or components given in a lattice basis), the property has a convention or basis subproperty, required as stated in its description. Conversion factors to SI for units not exactly defined in SI terms (bohr, hartree, Ry) are those of CODATA 2022, as listed in Annex U.

A1.2 In the same bullet list, after the "Values:" bullet, add two new bullets:

  • Quantity kind: The physical dimension of the Property's value, given as a MatCore quantity-kind name mapped to a QUDT QuantityKind IRI in Annex U (e.g. Energy, Length, InverseLength, Temperature, Pressure). Reserved values: dimensionless (ratios, counts), inapplicable (strings, identifiers, and the unit subproperty itself), any (the value of a generic name/value/unit parameter, whose quantity kind is then given by the instance unit).
  • Recommended unit: The unit customarily used for this Property in the community. Informative only; used by templates and tools.

A1.3 Add to the paragraph beginning "Examples are provided after each Standard specification in XML format":

In the XML examples, unit, convention and basis are written as attributes of the value element for brevity; an equivalent child-element serialization is also conformant.

Subproperties: unit (required) cell Standard units: meter (m) Quantity kind: Length. Recommended unit: angstrom. Subproperties: unit (required; applies to all nine components) cell-reference Standard units: meter (m) Same as cell cell-periodicity Standard units: dimensionless Quantity kind: inapplicable (booleans) temperature Standard units: kelvin (K) Quantity kind: Temperature. Recommended unit: K. Subproperties: unit (required) stress Standard units: pascal (Pa) Quantity kind: Pressure. Recommended unit: GPa. A7.1 domain-size (line ~636): replace

An ordered list of real numbers containing the domain dimensions in meters (m).

docs.text: A8.1 Apply A3.2 to calculation-parameter > unit* (line ~844); add Quantity kind: any to its value* row.

docs.title: A9. New Annex U — MatCore Unit Table
docs.text:
Insert the contents of the separate file MatCore_Annex_U_Unit_Table.md as a new section after §2.7 (or as an appendix), keeping its heading "Annex U — MatCore Unit Table (Normative)". It contains the rules, the quantity-kind table, the unit-symbol table, seven explanatory notes and a references list, and all identifiers and factors in it have been verified against the QUDT v3.3.0 source, GNU Units 2.23 (definitions.units v3.19) and NIST CODATA 2022.

Two consequences for other entries in this list:

  • Annex U defines MolarEnergy as a quantity kind distinct from Energy (Rule 8). Any typed MD property that is conventionally reported per mole should be declared with Quantity kind MolarEnergy and recommended unit kJ/mol or kcal/mol, not Energy.
  • Annex U Rule 4 pins x-gnu: expressions to GNU Units 2.23 / definitions.units v3.19; the wording in A3.2 needs no change since it refers to Annex U.

docs.title: A10. Update the XML examples
docs.text:
A10.1 In every example, add unit="…" to each dimensioned value, e.g.

<temperature unit="K">300</temperature>
<kinetic-energy-cutoff unit="eV">520</kinetic-energy-cutoff>
<k-point-spacing unit="1/angstrom" convention="2pi-included">0.25</k-point-spacing>

A10.2 In the existing generic-parameter examples (lines ~720–780), <unit>dimensionless</unit> is already conformant; leave as is. Check that any non-dimensionless examples use an Annex U symbol.

docs.title: A11. Version note
docs.text:
Add to the preamble or a changelog:

From version X, unit is required on all dimensioned properties. Files declaring an earlier MatCore version are interpreted using the fixed units of that version (Annex U, legacy table).

If a legacy table is kept, populate it from the Standard units values removed in A2–A8.

docs.title: PART B — Fixes to existing content
docs.text:
These are corrections independent of the units design.

B1. temperature-gradient (line 143). Old: Standard units: watts per square meter (K/m). The name is wrong; the symbol is right. Under Part A this row is replaced by A2.2; if applying B1 alone, change to kelvin per meter (K/m).

B2. planewave-basis-cutoff vs kinetic-energy-cutoff (line 495 vs 276). The MBPT entry says the quantity "is the same as the kinetic energy cutoff" but gives Ry while the DFT entry gives eV. Under Part A both become explicit-unit Energy properties (A3.1, A5); if applying B2 alone, align on one unit. Consider adding: "Note: If the DFT kinetic-energy-cutoff is given, this value should agree with it."

B3. exciton-momentum (line 506). Old: Standard units: Reciprocal lattice units (2π/a). This is a convention, not a unit, and "2π/a" presumes a cubic cell. Replace with the basis subproperty wording in A5. If applying B3 alone, at minimum change to "Values: components in fractions of the reciprocal lattice vectors (dimensionless)".

B4. strain-rate (line 141). Old: Standard units: dimensionless. A rate has dimension 1/time. Replace per A2.2; if applying alone, change to inverse seconds (1/s). Also, the Values sentence uses the symbol E for the strain-rate tensor, the same symbol the strain entry (line 140) uses for the strain tensor; suggest Ė (or dE/dt) for the strain rate.

B5. shift (line 283). Old: Standard units: 1/angstrom (1/Å). A mesh shift is customarily a fraction of the mesh spacing (e.g. 0.5 for a half-shift), which is dimensionless. Confirm with the entry's author; if fractional, apply A3.1; if it is an absolute offset in reciprocal length, keep InverseLength and add the same convention subproperty as k-point-spacing.

B6. SCF tolerance (line 289). Old: "Convergence criterion for the self-consistent loop … Standard units: electron Volt (eV)". Codes converge on energy, charge density, or potential, and the unit depends on which. Add the criterion subproperty per A3.1; if applying alone, at least say "Convergence criterion (on total energy) for the self-consistent loop".

B7. k-point-spacing (line 282). The entry states 1/angstrom (1/Å) but does not say whether the factor 2π is included, and codes differ. Under Part A this is handled by the required convention subproperty in A3.1; if applying alone, add a note: "State whether the factor 2π is included in the reciprocal length."

B8. Naming consistency. The draft uses unit (singular) throughout; keep it that way in all new text and avoid "units" as a field name. Normalize "Dimensionless." (capital D, line 286) to "dimensionless" wherever it remains.

B9. Generic quadruple definitions. All unit* rows share the definition "A standardized string or identifier that defines the dimension or measurement system of the associated value." Suggest: "The unit in which the associated value is expressed."

B10. cell-periodicity (line 137). Marked Standard units: dimensionless but the values are booleans; under Part A becomes inapplicable (A2.2). If applying alone, delete the units phrase.

B11. free-energy > unit (line 666). Definition says "free energy density" but expression may be a total free energy; reworded in A7.3.

B12. Annex U CODATA version. Superseded: the published Annex U states CODATA 2022 explicitly and its factors have been verified; no action needed.

docs.title: 0002 — Replace the prose "Values" field with typed fields
docs.text: Date: 2026-09-28. Status: accepted (implementation pending).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Each property has type (string|float|int|bool|file|any), extent (KIM notation; any for generic parameters), kind (Annex U kinds or dimensionless|inapplicable|any), recommended-unit, structured values, required, repeatable. "Kind" rather than "Quantity kind". Generic name/value/unit/description parameters: value is type any, extent any, kind any; instance supplies type/shape/unit. repeatable (property may occur more than once) is distinct from an open extent (shape of one value).

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: Machine-readable fields allow XSD/JSON Schema and the unit validator to be generated from the YAML. Follows OpenKIM Property Definitions and OPTIMADE property definitions.

docs.title: 0003 — scaling subproperty for nondimensional phase-field lengths and times
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-31. Status: accepted. Decided by: Ellad Tadmor.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Phase-field simulations are often run in nondimensional units (e.g. grid spacing 1, time step 0.01). Under 0001, domain-size and grid-spacing have Kind Length and time-step-size has Kind Time, and Annex U Rule 3 forbids dimensionless for a dimensioned Kind, so nondimensional values would be non-conformant.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• domain-size, grid-spacing and time-step-size each have a required subproperty scaling with enum [physical, nondimensional].
  • When scaling = physical, unit SHALL be an Annex U symbol of the property's Kind (Length, or Time for time-step-size).
  • When scaling = nondimensional, unit SHALL be dimensionless.
  • Recommended units (informative): m for domain-size and grid-spacing, s for time-step-size.
  • Note for each of the three properties: the characteristic length and time scales used for the nondimensionalization should be recorded as model-parameter entries so the values can be interpreted.
  • The validator checks this conditional rule.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Nondimensional phase-field data are conformant, and the unit check still applies to physical data. This is the first rule in which the allowed unit depends on the value of another subproperty; it has the same shape as the convention rule for k-point-spacing (0001 A3.1).

docs.title: 0004 — Rulings on the CLAUDE.md audit
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-31. Status: accepted. Decided by: Ellad Tadmor.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: CLAUDE.md stated a number of rules that no decision record backed. Each was reviewed one by one and ruled a decision, a proposal, or a correction. Rulings recorded elsewhere are not repeated here: the A3.3 removal (0001), the generic-parameter groups and the Annex U Rule 4 amendment (0001), and phase-field scaling (0003).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
1. Status of 0001. Part A is accepted. In Part B, B1, B3, B4 (the unit), B6, B7, B8, B10 and B11 are accepted; B2 (the added note), B4 (the Ė symbol), B5 and B9 are proposals awaiting a decision; B12 needs no action. A6 is a proposal.
  2. GitHub organization. The repository stays at matcore-standard/matcore. The name matcore is held by a dormant personal account; a GitHub support request to contact the owner is pending and unlikely to succeed. If matcore is released, whether to move to it or point it at matcore-standard will be decided then.
  3. Repository URL. Only mkdocs.yml contains the repository URL. Other files link relative to the site or read it from mkdocs.yml.
  4. Baseline .docx. The frozen Google Doc export stays in docs/decisions/ and is excluded from the published site. It remains downloadable from the public repository itself.
  5. Schema YAML is regular. No YAML anchors or aliases, custom tags, includes or templating in schema files.
  6. Field set and order. Each property entry has exactly the fields name, required, description, type, extent, kind, recommended-unit, values, repeatable, [convention], [notes], [legacy_values], [legacy_unit], [subproperties], in that order. validate_schema.py will enforce the order.
  7. any is not limited to generic parameters. type, extent and kind may be any wherever the schema leaves the field open and something else fixes it: the instance (generic parameters) or a required enumerated subproperty (e.g. criterion for the SCF tolerance, basis for exciton-momentum).
  8. Extent notation. In YAML the open-length colon is quoted ([":"]); in prose and generated docs it is written [:].
  9. Inapplicable kinds. string, bool and file properties have kind inapplicable; a physical quantity is never typed as a string.
  10. Recommended unit. Informative only; it must be an Annex U symbol whose kind matches the property's kind.
  11. Structured values. values is structured and replaces the prose "Values" (0002). Its key set is a proposal.
  12. legacy_* fields. The baseline prose is kept in legacy_* fields during migration and deleted once its content is transferred to the typed fields. The original wording remains in the baseline .docx and in git history (tag v0.9-baseline). A section is complete when no legacy_* fields remain.
  13. Names. Names match ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$. A name is plural only when its value is a list (open extent); a repeatable property with a single value per occurrence stays singular. unit is singular.
  14. Terminology. "Annex" for Annex U, which is normative. "Kind", not "Quantity kind", in the schema, the standard's prose and new text. Decision records are not rewritten. "Quantity kind" remains where it refers to QUDT's concept.
  15. Funding. The MatCore effort is funded by NSF DMR Award #2404283 and supported through the KIM Initiative.
  16. Generic-parameter values (added 2026-10-31). The instance type of a generic parameter's value is one of float, int, string, bool, matching the baseline wording of all five generic parameters. The type is stated in the instance, not inferred from how the value is written; each serialization defines how it is written. The value need not be a scalar: its extent remains any (0002).
  17. Serialization (added 2026-10-31). §1.3 defines the term: "A serialization is a file format (for example XML or JSON) together with the rules that map the MatCore data model onto it." Elsewhere the term is used without naming formats.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: CLAUDE.md is updated to match, and every unbacked statement in it is marked PROPOSED, NOT DECIDED. Follow-up changes: exclude the .docx from the site build (4); tighten the name pattern in the meta-schema (13); add a field-order check to validate_schema.py (6); reword Annex U to "Kind" when 0001 Part A is applied (14).

docs.title: 0005 — Commit each ruling as it is made; the human pushes
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-31. Status: accepted. Decided by: Ellad Tadmor.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A ruling that exists only in a conversation is lost when the session ends, and batching several rulings into one change mixes unrelated edits in the same files.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• When the human rules on an item, the ruling is written into the repository (CLAUDE.md, plus a decision record where one is needed) before the next item is taken up.
  • The diff is shown to the human and committed once approved.
  • Claude never pushes. The human pushes, since every push to main redeploys the site.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Each ruling is a small, separately reviewable commit, and no ruling depends on the conversation surviving.

docs.title: 1.1 Objectives
docs.text:
The Material Core Metadata (MatCore)* *standard for computational materials science (CMS) represents key aspects of a material-focused computation to make it understandable to the broad materials research community. It provides pragmatic and workable guidelines for documentation of materials data.

The primary goals of the MatCore standard are, by outlining expectations for metadata accompanying a computational dataset, to facilitate: (1) dataset transparency, discoverability, sharing and reuse in theoretical and computational modeling, (2) verification and validation of materials modeling and simulation software, and (3) training physics-based and machine learning (ML) models for material behavior. An additional, more challenging, objective is to promote reproducibility in CMS by providing the information necessary for researchers to regenerate a published dataset.

docs.title: 1.2 Scope
docs.text:
The MatCore standard is focused on CMS methods aimed at computing material properties from a microscopic perspective, as opposed to computational methods in which the material is a component (such as engineering finite element analysis). The MatCore standard is designed to be flexible so that it can be extended to any area of CMS and can accommodate future changes in the field. An initial focus is placed on major CMS methods most widely used at the time of the creation of the standard with the aim of adding other methods in the future. The initial methods to be supported are:

  • DFT: Density functional theory

  • MD: Classical molecular dynamics

  • MBPT: Many-body perturbation theory (GW/BSE)

  • ML: Machine learning

  • PF: Phase field

  • DER: Derived properties from CMS calculations

All methods share a common minimal set of metadata defined by the MatCore standard. In addition, each method has its own MatCore extension, e.g. MatCore-DFT, MatCore-MD, etc., that inherits from the minimal MatCore metadata and adds additional method-specific metadata.

It is allowable to include multiple method-specific metadata if used in concert. For example, an ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) dataset could include both MatCore-DFT and MatCore-MD metadata files to document both aspects of the computation.

docs.title: 1.3 Format
docs.text:
Each standard consists of a set of Properties with possible SubProperties, SubSubProperties, etc. The term “Property” will be used in the rest of this section to refer collectively to Property, SubProperty, etc. Properties have the following characteristics:

  • Each Property has a name consisting of a series of one or more words all in lower case separated by hyphens.

  • Required Properties are indicated by an asterisk (*) appended to the end of the Property name.

  • Properties have the following features:

  • Definition: A short explanation of the nature of the Property. Best-practice is to not use words from the Property name in the definition to prevent circular definitions, except in cases where confusion is unlikely.

  • Values: A description of the type of variable (string, integer, real), form (scalar, list, array), and possible values that the Property can take on.

  • When appropriate a controlled vocabulary can be defined. In this case sentence case format is adopted (i.e. for a phrase containing several words, the first letter of the first word is capitalized and all others are lower case except for proper names or acronyms). An option should always be added for users to add terms not included in the controlled vocabulary to allow the standard to support future developments. New terms may eventually be standardized and added to the controlled vocabulary.

  • When a controlled vocabulary is used, adoption of existing standards is recommended whenever possible.

  • When a value has physical units, either the required unit must be specified, or a field provided to define the value units.

  • For Properties that contain SubProperties, this is indicated with the phrase “Contains SubProperties as defined in the table below” (where “table below” points to the specification for the SubProperty standard).

  • Repeatable: A boolean variable that is “True” for Properties that may appear multiple times inside the metadata file. For example, for a dataset created by more than one person, the creator Property can be repeated as many times as needed, each with its own SubProperties.

  • Note(s): Additional clarifying information regarding a Property.

In addition to the required and optional Properties, other arbitrary Properties can be added to any MatCore Standard metadata files to support developments in the field. Such Properties may eventually be standardized and added to the MatCore Standard.

Examples are provided after each Standard specification in XML format. However, this is for clarification purposes only. The MatCore Standard serves as a conceptual and logical framework. It defines the schema for Properties required to ensure data consistency and interoperability. Critically, the MatCore Standard is implementation-agnostic. It dictates what information must be captured and how it should be structured logically, but it does not mandate a specific substrate, file format, or programming language.

A serialization is a file format (for example XML or JSON) together with the rules that map the MatCore data model onto it.

MatCore adopts Semantic Versioning (SemVer) three-part versioning system (major, minor, patch) to indicate Standard changes.

docs.title: 2.1 Minimal MatCore Metadata
docs.text: * = required property

docs.title: creator*
docs.text:
An entity (e.g. person, organization, software agent) responsible for generated the dataset and their institutional affiliation if relevant.

Repeatable: True

Values (legacy text): Contains SubProperties as listed below.

The name of the entity that generated the dataset.

docs.title: creation-date*
docs.text:
The calendar date and time when the dataset was created.

docs.title: description*
docs.text:
A synopsis of the dataset, its contents, and purpose.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing a description of the dataset contents. This can optionally include information on the format in which the dataset is stored (e.g. pointer to a relevant schema).

docs.title: disclaimer
docs.text:
A statement of applicability provided by the creator(s) informing users of the intended use and/or limitations of this dataset.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the dataset disclaimer.

docs.title: material-component*
docs.text:
A description of the chemical composition and structure of a substance in this dataset.

Repeatable: True

Values (legacy text): Contains SubProperties as listed below.

docs.title: constituent*
docs.text:
A chemical element included in the material component and its concentration.

Repeatable: True

Values (legacy text): Contains SubSubProperties as defined in the table below.

docs.title: species*
docs.text:
A chemical element included in the material.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the chemical designation of the element (e.g. "C").

docs.title: concentration*
docs.text:
The fraction of the material composed of this element.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the concentration in percent.

docs.title: phase*
docs.text:
The phase of the material included in the dataset.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A list of strings containing one or more of the following values: "Amorphous" – A solid material without crystalline order "Crystal" – A solid material characterized by a repeating pattern of atoms. "Quasicrystal" – A crystal-like material with short-range order, but without long-range order. "Molecule" – A finite group of atoms bonded together forming an independent unit. "Liquid" – A fluid structure (e.g. the molten state of a material) "Gas" – A structure where atoms are far apart and only interact during collisions. "Plasma" – A gas comprised of ions and electrons. Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

docs.title: description
docs.text:
An explanation of the nature of the material, e.g. a crystal structure designation, a chemical formula for a molecule, etc.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the material description.

docs.title: microstructure
docs.text:
The arrangement of phases, grains and defects in a material.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing a description of the microstructure of the material.

docs.title: computation*
docs.text:
A description of a computer simulation used to generate data in the dataset.

Repeatable: True

Values (legacy text): Contains SubProperties as listed below.

docs.title: method-class*
docs.text:
The general category to which the computational technique belongs.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing one of the following values: "Electronic" "Atomistic" "Mesoscopic" "Continuum" "Data-driven" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

Note:The categories listed above are based on the MODA standard.

docs.title: method*
docs.text:
The computational materials science (CMS) approach used in the computation.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing one of the following values: For method-class "Electronic": "CC" – Coupled Cluster "QMC" – Quantum Monte Carlo "DFT" – Density Functional Theory "MBPT" – Many-Body Perturbation Theory methods (such as GW and BSE) For method-class "Atomistic": "MC" – Monte Carlo "MD" – Molecular Dynamics For method-class "Mesoscopic": "DDD" – Discrete Dislocation Dynamics "KMC" – Kinetic Monte Carlo "CGMD" – Coarse-grained MD For method-class "Continuum": "PF" – Phase Field For method-class "Data-driven": "ML" – Machine Learning Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

docs.title: simulation-conditions*
docs.text:
The interactions between the system being modeled and the rest of the world maintained during the computation.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): Contains SubSubProperties as defined in the table below.

docs.title: type*
docs.text:
The nature of the simulation being performed, whether equilibrium, nonequilibrium, or nonstandard.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): String containing one of the following values defining the simulation conditions: "Equilibrium" – Thermodynamic equilibrium "Nonequilibrium" – Conforming to some definition of nonequilibrium thermodynamics "Other" – A simulation not fitting into the equilibrium and nonequilibrium categories. Note 1: The SubSubProperties listed below (aside from description) are provided as appropriate given the nature of the simulation. Providing a SubSubProperty means that its value is imposed on the simulation as an external constraint. Note 2:Units for dimensioned variables are to be given in the SI unit system.

docs.title: description
docs.text:
Explanatory text clarifying the simulation type selection.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the simulation type explanation.

docs.title: number-of-particles
docs.text:
A count of atoms or other discrete entities comprising the material.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): An integer containing the number of particles N.

Standard units (legacy text): dimensionless

docs.title: volume
docs.text:
The amount of space occupied by the material.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A real number containing the volume V.

Standard units (legacy text): cubic meters (m^3)

docs.title: mass-density
docs.text:
The total mass of the material divided by the volume it occupies.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A real number containing the mass density 𝜌.

Standard units (legacy text): kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m^3)

docs.title: number-density
docs.text:
The total number of particles comprising the material divided by the volume it occupies.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A real number containing the number density n.

Standard units (legacy text): inverse cubic meter (1/m^3)

docs.title: cell
docs.text:
The domain occupied by the material in the simulation (if fixed).

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): Ordered list of three vectors (a, b, c), each with three components, that define the simulation cell. The vectors (a, b, c) need not be orthogonal, and the magnitudes (│a│, │b│, │c│) are the supercell vector lengths.

Standard units (legacy text): meter (m)

docs.title: cell-reference
docs.text:
The domain occupied by the material in the simulation in configuration relative to which strains are defined.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): Ordered list of three vectors (a0, b0, c0), each with three components, that define the cell used in the simulation in its reference configuration. The vectors (a0, b0, c0) need not be orthogonal, and the magnitudes (│a0│, │b0│, │c0│) are the reference cell vector lengths.

Standard units (legacy text): meter (m)

docs.title: cell-periodicity
docs.text:
Specification of whether periodic boundary conditions are applied along the cell vector directions. This applies to both cell and cell-reference.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): Ordered list of three booleans (pa,, pb,, pc,), which are set to true if periodic boundary conditions are applied along the corresponding cell vectors (a, b, c).

Standard units (legacy text): dimensionless

docs.title: temperature
docs.text:
A measure of the hotness or coldness of an external heat bath in thermal contact with the material.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A real number containing the temperature T.

Standard units (legacy text): kelvin (K)

docs.title: stress
docs.text:
A uniform force per unit current area, including both normal and shear components, applied to the material during the simulation through contact with an external loading device.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): An array of six real numbers containing the components of the (symmetric) Cauchy stress tensor σ in the following order: [σ11, σ22, σ33, σ23, σ13, σ12]. The stress component are expressed relative to an orthonormal basis (e1, e2, e3), where e1 is in the direction of a, e2 is in the direction of c╳a, and e3= e1╳e2, where (a, b, c) are the vectors defining the cell, which may not be orthogonal. Note 1: Requires the definition of the cell subproperty in order for a basis to be defined relative to which the tensor components are given. Note 2:The adopted sign convention is for tensile normal stresses to be positive, and compressive normal stresses to be negative. This implies that for a material subjected to a positive pressure p, the stress tensor components are [-p, -p, -p, 0, 0, 0].

Standard units (legacy text): pascal (Pa)

docs.title: strain
docs.text:
A deformation relative to a reference configuration imposed on the simulation cell expressed in the referential frame (Lagrangian strain tensor).

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): An array of six real numbers containing the components of the (symmetric) Lagrangian strain tensor Ein the following order: [E11, E22, E33, E23, E13, E12]. The strain component are expressed relative to an orthonormal basis (e1, e2, e3), where e1 is in the direction of a0, e2 is in the direction of c0╳a0, and e3= e1╳e2, where (a0, b0, c0) are the vectors defining the cell in the reference configuration, which may not be orthogonal. Note: Requires the definition of cell-reference in order for the basis to be defined relative to which the tensor components are given.

Standard units (legacy text): dimensionless

docs.title: strain-rate
docs.text:
The derivative with respect to time of a deformation relative to a reference configuration imposed on the simulation cell expressed in the referential frame (Lagrangian strain rate tensor), which is constant throughout the simulation.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): An array of six real numbers containing the components of the (symmetric) Lagrangian strain rate tensor E in the following order: [E11, E22, E33, E23, E13, E12,]. The strain component are expressed relative to an orthonormal basis (e1, e2, e3), where e1 is in the direction of a0, e2 is in the direction of c0╳a0, and e3= e1╳e2, where (a0, b0, c0) are the vectors defining the cell in the reference configuration, which may not be orthogonal.

Standard units (legacy text): dimensionless

Requires the definition of cell-reference in order for the basis to be defined relative to which the tensor components are given

docs.title: heat-flux
docs.text:
The amount of thermal energy transferred to the material per unit area per unit time along a given direction.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): An array of three real numbers containing the components of the heat flux vector q. The heat flux component are expressed relative to an orthonormal basis (e1, e2, e3), where e1 is in the direction of a, e2 is in the direction of c╳a, and e3= e1╳e2, where (a, b, c) are the vectors defining the cell, which may not be orthogonal.

Standard units (legacy text): watts per square meter (W/m^2)

docs.title: temperature-gradient
docs.text:
A physical quantity that describes the rate and direction of maximum temperature change per unit distance.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): An array of three real numbers containing the components of the temperature gradient vector ∇T. The temperature gradient component are expressed relative to an orthonormal basis (e1, e2, e3), where e1 is in the direction of a, e2 is in the direction of c╳a, and e3= e1╳e2, where (a, b, c) are the vectors defining cell, which may not be orthogonal.

Standard units (legacy text): watts per square meter (K/m)

docs.title: link

docs.title: citation

Information that uniquely identifies a source being acknowledged.

docs.title: reference*

Text that uniquely identifies the source of information being cited.

docs.title: doi

The digital object identifier (DOI) for the source.

Information about received monetary support or other resources to generate the dataset.

Other datasets that are connected to the current one in some manner.

"Version update" – Change to the dataset or associated files requiring a new version "Metadata update" – Change to the metadata, but not the dataset itself. Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

docs.title: date*
docs.text:
The date and time when the change was made.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the creation date in either format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssz (where "z" indicates UTC time zone) format (following the ISO 8601 Date and Time Format Standard).

docs.title: agent*

The calendar date and time when this MatCore document was created.

Values (legacy text): A string containing the creation date in either format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssz (where "z" indicates UTC time zone) format (following the ISO 8601 Date and Time Format Standard).

docs.title: license*

docs.title: 2.2 DFT
docs.text: * = required property

docs.title: xc-functional*
docs.text:
Approximation used to describe the electron exchange and electron correlation energies

Repeatable: True

Values (legacy text): Contains SubProperties as listed below.

docs.title: type*
docs.text:
The mathematical form of the exchange-correlation functional.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): String containing one of the following values: "LDA" – Local Density Approximation "GGA" – Generalized Gradient Approximation "Meta GGA" – Extension to GGA including dependence on Laplacian of electron density "Hybrid" – An approximation for the exchange-correlation (XC) functional that includes a portion of the exact XC from Hartree–Fock theory or machine learning with the rest coming from other sources (ab initio or empirical). "ML" – Machine learning based functional Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

docs.title: description
docs.text:
Explanatory text providing more information about the type of the exchange-correlation method used including any relevant identifying information.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing more information about the exchange-correlation type. Examples of possible content by type: LDA: Common parameterizations: VMN, PW92, etc. GGA: Typical choices are PW91, PBE, rPBE, revPBE, BLYP, etc. Meta GGA: Specific named examples include TPSS, SCAN, M06, etc. Hybrid: B3LYP, PBE0, HSE03, HSE06, NeuralXC, DeePKS, … ML: DM21, NNLDA, NNGGA, CIDER, etc. others: BEEF, VdW-corrections (added on top of XC, e.g., D2, D3, D4), etc. LibXC designation: LibXC:LDA_C_GK72 (include source as prefix)

docs.title: xc-parameter
docs.text:
A fixed variable associated with the specified exchange-correlation functional method.

Repeatable: True

Values (legacy text): Contains SubSubProperties as defined in the table below.

docs.title: name*
docs.text:
The designation of the exchange-correlation parameter.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the name of an exchange-correlation parameter.

docs.title: value*
docs.text:
The data associated with the exchange-correlation parameter.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): An integer, real, boolean, or string containing the parameter value.

docs.title: unit*
docs.text:
A standardized string or identifier that defines the dimension or measurement system of the associated value.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the units of the value in the GNU unit convention (or the text "dimensionless").

docs.title: description
docs.text:
An explanation of the meaning, source, or purpose of the parameter.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string explaining the exchange-correlation parameter. This can be the mixing parameter for a hybrid exchange-correlation, or other method-specific parameters.

docs.title: core-electron-model*

Model of the electrons used in the calculation.

Repeatable: False

docs.title: type*

The method used to model the electrons.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): String containing one of the following values: "All Electron" – All of the electrons in an atom are modeled explicitly. "LAPW" – "Linearized Augmented Plane Wave" "Pseudopotential" – Valence electrons are treated explicitly, and core electrons are modeled by a simplified potential. "PAW" – Projector Augmented Wave Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

docs.title: name*

The name of the pseudopotential.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the pseudopotential name.

docs.title: type*
docs.text:
The physical form of the pseudopotential.

docs.title: description
docs.text:
Explanatory text about the pseudopotential including any relevant identifying information.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): A string containing the pseudopotential description.

docs.title: number-of-valence-electrons*

docs.title: repository

docs.title: version

docs.title: doi
docs.text:

Values (legacy text): A string containing the pseudopotential DOI.

docs.title: unique-identifier

Repeatable: False

docs.title: valence-electron-model*

The elementary functions used for expanding electronic wave functions.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): Contains SubProperties as listed below.

docs.text:
The choice of a basis set to expand electronic wave functions.

docs.title: localized-orbital-basis-set

docs.title: type*

docs.title: repository
docs.text:
The database from which the localized-orbital basis set was obtained.

docs.title: version

The version of the localized-orbital basis set.

docs.title: doi
docs.text:

docs.title: unique-identifier

docs.title: calculation-physics

docs.title: k-point-mesh
docs.text:
For periodic systems, a grid of points sampled within the Brillouin zone, used to approximate integrals and calculate electronic properties by discretizing the wavefunction across reciprocal space.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): Contains SubProperties as listed below.

docs.title: type*
docs.text:
The choice of how k-points are distributed on the mesh.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): String containing one of the following values: "Monkhorst-Pack" "Gamma centered" "Irregular" Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

docs.title: number-of-points
docs.text:
How many k-points are included along each reciprocal lattice vector.

Values (legacy text): Ordered list of three integer numbers containing the number k-points along the three reciprocal lattice vector directions.

Standard units (legacy text): dimensionless

docs.title: k-point-spacing
docs.text:
Separation between k-points along each reciprocal lattice vector direction.

Repeatable: False

docs.title: self-consistency*
docs.text:
Specifies the level of iterative updating applied to the Green's function (G), the screened Coulomb interaction (W), or the excitonic Hamiltonian during the calculation. This property identifies whether the MBPT equations are solved in a 'one-shot' perturbative manner or through an iterative cycle where the electronic or excitonic quasiparticle states are updated to reach a self-consistent solution.

Repeatable: False

Values (legacy text): String containing one of the following values depending on the variant of the GW, BSE, or GW/BSE approach used: "G0W0" – One-shot calculation; the G and *W *are constructed using the starting eigenvalues and wavefunctions. "GW0" – Only the Green's function G is updated iteratively, while *W *remains fixed at the *W0 *level "G0W" – Only the screened interaction W is updated iteratively, while G remains fixed at G0 "scGW" – Fully self-consistent GW; bothG* and W are updated iteratively until the quasiparticle energies and/or wavefunctions converge "QSGW" – Quasiparticle self-consistent GW; the starting potential is updated to provide the optimal independent particle basis for the GW expansion "BSE0" – One-shot BSE; the excitonic Hamiltonian is built once using fixed GW quasiparticle energies and screening (W) "scBSE" – Self-consistent BSE; internal refinement of the kernel or energies within the BSE process "evGW+BSE" – Eigenvalue-only self-consistent GW (evGW) used as the starting point for a subsequent BSE calculation "scGW+BSE" – The BSE is solved using the results of a fully self-consistent GW calculation Other user-specified value if none of the above apply.

docs.title: Annex U — MatCore Unit Table
docs.text:
(Normative)

Amended 2026-10-31: Rule 4 extended from generic parameters to any subproperty whose Kind the schema declares as any (see decision 0001).

docs.title: U.1 Purpose
docs.text:
This annex defines the closed set of unit symbols that MAY appear as the value of a unit subproperty in a MatCore metadata instance, the quantity kind of each symbol, and its conversion to coherent SI. It also defines the quantity-kind names used in the Quantity kind field of the schema and their mapping to the QUDT ontology.

A validator checks that (a) the symbol is in Table U.4 and (b) its quantity kind matches the quantity kind declared for the property in the schema. No unit parsing is required.

docs.title: U.2 Rules
docs.text:
1. Symbols are case-sensitive ASCII strings. eV and ev are not the same symbol.
  2. Compound symbols use / for division and ^ for integer exponents, exactly as written in Table U.4. Symbols not listed (e.g. eV/A, Å, angstrom**3) are non-conformant.
  3. The reserved symbol dimensionless is used for quantities of dimension one (ratios, counts, fractional coordinates). It SHALL NOT be used for plane angles (use rad or degree) or for amount of substance (use mol).
  4. A unit subproperty of a generic parameter or of any other subproperty whose Kind the schema declares as any MAY, if and only if no symbol in Table U.4 applies, contain a string of the form x-gnu:<expression>, where <expression> is a unit expression valid in GNU Units 2.23 with definitions.units version 3.19 (February 2024). Such values are accepted with a validation warning and are not guaranteed to be machine-convertible. Later versions of definitions.units are not implied; a change of the pinned version is a revision of this annex.
  5. Conversion factors marked exact follow from the SI definitions. Factors marked CODATA 2022 are the 2022 CODATA recommended values published by NIST. The factors in Table U.4 are normative for MatCore and take precedence over the values embedded in any external vocabulary (see Note 5). A revision to a later CODATA release is a revision of this annex.
  6. This annex is versioned with the standard. Instance files SHALL use symbols from the annex version matching their declared MatCore version. Symbols are only ever added; a symbol, once published, is never removed or redefined.
  7. Compatibility between a unit and a quantity kind is decided by the SI dimension vector in Table U.3, not by QUDT's own hasQuantityKind links (see Note 4).
  8. Energy and MolarEnergy are distinct quantity kinds and are not interchangeable. A property declared with Quantity kind Energy SHALL NOT carry a MolarEnergy unit, and vice versa (see Note 1).

Note 1 (molar energies). kJ/mol, kcal/mol and J/mol are units of energy per amount of substance and belong to the quantity kind MolarEnergy, consistent with QUDT, which links these units to quantitykind:MolarEnergy. They are the customary energy units of classical force fields, and properties in the MD section that are conventionally reported per mole are declared with Quantity kind MolarEnergy. Conversion between Energy and MolarEnergy is a division or multiplication by the Avogadro constant (6.022 140 76 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, exact) and is a task for tooling, not for a unit value.

Note 2 (2π convention). InverseLength symbols do not encode whether a factor 2π is included. Properties for which this matters (e.g. k-point-spacing) carry a separate required convention subproperty.

Note 3 (mole vs. dimensionless). Following OPTIMADE, dimensionless SHALL NOT be used for amounts of substance or plane angles.

Note 4 (QUDT quantity-kind links are not a validation basis). QUDT attaches its own quantity kinds to units, and these are often narrower or differently named than MatCore's: PER-SEC is linked to Frequency and DecayConstant (not InverseTime); PER-M3 to InverseVolume (not NumberDensity); W-PER-M2 to PowerPerArea (not HeatFluxDensity); GigaPA, KiloBAR and BAR to ForcePerArea (not Pressure); EV-PER-ANGSTROM to TotalLinearStoppingPower (not Force). In every case the dimension vector agrees with the MatCore quantity kind, so compatibility is validated by dimension vector (Rule 7), and the QUDT unit IRI serves only as a stable identifier.

Note 5 (stale constants in reference vocabularies). QUDT's own conversion multipliers for E_h (4.359 743 94 × 10⁻¹⁸ J) and AMU (1.660 538 782 83 × 10⁻²⁷ kg) are CODATA 2006 values, and GNU Units 2.23 uses CODATA 2018 values (hartree 4.359 744 722 2071 × 10⁻¹⁸ J, bohrradius 5.291 772 109 02 × 10⁻¹¹ m, amu 1.660 539 066 6 × 10⁻²⁷ kg). The factors in Table U.4 are therefore normative in MatCore (Rule 5) and take precedence over the values embedded in either reference vocabulary.

Note 6 (GNU spelling of bohr). GNU Units does not define bohr; the GNU name is bohrradius. The MatCore symbol remains bohr; the mapping is given in the GNU column.

Note 7 (units absent from QUDT). Ry, bohr, meV, nm^3, 1/ps, 1/bohr, bohr^3, K/angstrom, eV/angstrom^3, hartree/bohr and 1/angstrom^3 have no unit IRI in QUDT Units v3.3.0. For these, the MatCore symbol is the identifier and the quantity-kind IRI in Table U.3 supplies the semantic anchor. QUDT accepts contributions through its public repository, and IRIs will be added to this table if and when they are published.
